## Heated sick wagons, cooking equipment and hot tea

**Sources on this page:** p212 A1, p212 A5.

**Related source pages:** [p213 A6](213.md#source-p213-a6), [p213 A7](213.md#source-p213-a7).

<a id="edition-cases-military-medical-return-transports-heated-sick-wagons-cooking-equipment-and-hot-tea"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs pp212–213, 22 November 1918; published `Nov22-24` key, unchanged. [Inputs](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/inputs.json), [exact certificates](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/certificates.json), [method and limits](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/README.md).

The readable medical passages concern preparations for transports coming through from Turkey. They recommend a sick wagon fitted with stoves, cooking equipment and continuously available hot tea. The final paragraph asks for action as far as possible from Constantinople because the received place `NIKOLA9EW` may lack sufficient capacity. The text records recommendations and a forwarding request, not proof that the equipment or supplies were provided.

The source has a nominal seven-part frame. Parts 2 and 4 were retained as unassigned context in this medical package and are excluded from its restored-reading count. A subsequent [cross-copy audit](#edition-cases-caucasus-p212-p218-crosscopy) identifies the printed part 2 as a truncated copy of a separate Caucasus/Russia withdrawal message on p218. The [conditional part-4 edition](#edition-cases-military-p212-medical-fragment) now recovers 129/151 positions in its primary reading and 148/151 in an optional transport-doctor reading. The latter fills 102 missing coordinates without changing an observed coordinate; the 302-coordinate frame remains a hypothesis, and three opening positions remain unresolved. An unnumbered oil-cartel query between them is [edited separately](#edition-cases-finance-oil-cartel-dispatch-query). The relation of the seven printed parts remains unresolved.

### Attribution and retained gaps

The sick-wagon and final medical passages already had recognizable unreviewed repository candidates. This edition records the exact source and all local repairs; it makes no first historical decipherment claim. The two initially unassigned frames and all four tied first-part geometries remain preserved in this package's frozen evidence; the later part-2 identification has its own certificate and counting scope. No baseline square or later-period relabeling is applied to the medical readings.

## p212 A2 — Truncated cross-copy of the Tiflis armistice-withdrawal notice

**Edition context:** A truncated copy of the Tiflis armistice notice.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-p212-p218-crosscopy-a-truncated-copy-of-the-tiflis-armistice-notice"></a>



**Source edition and cross-copy analysis: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Newly edited record: Childs p212 A2. Earlier full witness: p218 A2, already in the [Tiflis armistice edition](218.md#edition-cases-caucasus-p218-a). Published `Nov25-28` key, unchanged. [Inputs](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/inputs.json), [exact certificate](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/certificates.json), [method and limits](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/README.md).

The fragment is part of the previously known notice concerning withdrawal from territory that belonged to Russia before the war and the Allies' assessment of its internal situation. Its role is established by the close ciphertext correspondence with the complete p218 part, not by joining it to the medical passages printed around p212.

**The date conflict remains unresolved:** p212 is headed 22 November, while p218's full witness is headed and received 25 November. The edition changes neither date and makes no claim about the cause of the discrepancy.

<a id="source-p212-a2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-p212-p218-crosscopy-p212-a2"></a>

### p212 A2

[Short-fragment source crop](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/sources/p212_A2.png); [full p218 A2 witness](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/sources/p218_A2.png). The p212 source advertises 284 coordinates but prints 160. Of those, 157 are identical to the corresponding p218 prefix. The differences are source indices 46 (`F/G`), 67 (`A/printed dash`) and 103 (`G/X`).

In the 284-coordinate frame, with the absent tail left as 124 erasures, only 30 plaintext positions have both source coordinates visible:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 284-slot frame with 124 absent tail coordinates left unknown:**

```text
?????????K??E????U??L?N?????????N??A????S??A?D?????????R??7????R??R?E?????????U??D????N??E?L?????????G??I????E??U?E?????????R??K????N??A?H????
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-p212-p218-crosscopy-a-conditional-tail-from-the-full-printed-witness"></a>

#### A conditional tail from the full printed witness

Borrowing p218's 124 literal tail coordinates, while preserving every p212 coordinate, gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional cross-copy tail completion from p218:**

```text
DIEVORDEMKRIEGZURUSZLANDGEHOERTENXHABENXSOBALDDIEALLIIERTE7UNTERBERUECKSICHTIGUNGDERJNNERENLAGEDIESERGEBIETEDENAUGENBLICKFUERGEKOMMENERACHTENX
```

</details>

This is a **source-copy reconstruction**, not a reading derived from the fragment alone. All borrowed coordinates have individual provenance in the certificate. Exhausting the 161 possible positions of one contiguous 124-coordinate loss gives the tail placement a unique minimum of two valid-coordinate disagreements. That supports the alignment under the copy assumption; it does not prove that an unseen historical tail was identical.

The copies are complementary. p212's F at index 46 independently supports the earlier `DPN → DEN` correction. Its A at index 67 supplies the missing coordinate in p218's `BERUEC?SICHTIGUNG`. In the other direction, p218's X at index 103 corrects p212's `ALLIIERTE7 → ALLIIERTEN`.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-p212-p218-crosscopy-conservative-readable-candidate"></a>

#### Conservative readable candidate

Using that one p218 witness correction in the observed p212 prefix, then separately changing borrowed coordinate 217 `X → F` for `JNNEREN → INNEREN`, gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conditional cross-copy tail completion, followed by the stated repairs:**

```text
DIEVORDEMKRIEGZURUSZLANDGEHOERTENXHABENXSOBALDDIEALLIIERTENUNTERBERUECKSICHTIGUNGDERINNERENLAGEDIESERGEBIETEDENAUGENBLICKFUERGEKOMMENERACHTENX
```

</details>

The received `RUSZLAND` spelling is retained. This is a continuation: “… die vor dem Krieg zu Russland gehörten, haben, sobald die Alliierten unter Berücksichtigung der inneren Lage dieser Gebiete den Augenblick für gekommen erachten …”. The surrounding withdrawal context belongs to the earlier complete three-part p218 notice; no complete p212 medical message is inferred.

Relative to p212's actual source, the candidate uses one observed-coordinate substitution and 124 missing-coordinate fills. Of those fills, 123 are literal p218 values; one is the explicitly separate ordinary-word correction. Thirty plaintext positions use two p212 coordinates, 100 use one coordinate from each copy, and 12 use only borrowed coordinates.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-p212-p218-crosscopy-the-neighboring-medical-fragment"></a>

### The neighboring medical fragment

p212 A4 now has a separate [conditional medical edition](#edition-cases-military-p212-medical-fragment): its primary reading fills 129/151 positions, and an optional transport-doctor reading reaches 148/151. Both depend on a proposed 302-coordinate frame; three positions in the opening remain unresolved.

The earlier copy search found no nonself exact ten-coordinate window among 788 frozen OCR blocks. That result is retained in this package's certificate. It concerns repeated source coordinates, not the later recovery within the proposed frame; the search did not span OCR block boundaries.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-p212-p218-crosscopy-attribution-and-scope"></a>

### Attribution and scope

The full p218 A2 body was already edited and catalogued; its earlier work is not recounted as a new message or a new physical record. The present contribution is recognition of the truncated p212 copy, a conditional tail restoration, and complementary source evidence for earlier repairs. Only p212 A2 is newly proposed for the catalog. No first historical decipherment or changed key/date is claimed.

**Edition context:** Oil cartel at Tiflis: details of shipments from Poti.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-oil-cartel-dispatch-query-oil-cartel-at-tiflis-details-of-shipments-from-poti"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs p212, 22 November 1918; published `Nov22-24` key, unchanged. [Source crop](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/sources/p212_A3.png), [inputs](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/inputs.json), [exact certificate](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/certificates.json).

This query asks the oil cartel at Tiflis to report when, where, to which address and by which ship their consignments were loaded from Poti. It does not provide the requested answers.

### p212 A3

The source prints `RICHI 224` but **no visible “3 TL” label**. `A3` is the catalog's positional identifier for the block between numbered parts 2 and 4. The query is kept separate from the surrounding medical passages; a shared subject or complete seven-part assembly is not assumed.

All 224 coordinates are observed. Raw, 112 positions:


An earlier unreviewed repository candidate already recognized the body. This edition adds literal source checking, all coordinate indices, full re-encryption and the explicit separation from the neighboring medical report. It does not claim first historical decipherment.

**Readable German — selected fragments only; literal 9 retained:**

> Lazarett […] Anstalten dorthin bekanntzugeben, wo Kranke verbleiben koennen […] Transport […] Personal […] Medikamenten zuteilen lassen und in9edem Zug.

**Conditional interpretation:** the fragments mention hospitals or institutions where sick people can remain and assigning medicines. The final phrase could mean “in every train” under the [separate globally injective J/numeral hypotheses](../../experiments/nov22_nikolajew_constraint/README.md). This edition retains `IN9EDEM` without a local square change. It does not establish that the described arrangements were implemented.

The joins remain uncertain. Received `3X`, the fully observed `9` at position 73, and opaque `YA`, `M` and `ER` are preserved. The selected `9` at position 143 requires one missing-half fill. The following [A5 starts EINEN…](#edition-cases-military-medical-return-transports-p212-a5), consistent with a continuation; it did not determine the new frame. The page also interposes an oil query and a [part-2 copy under another dated key](#edition-cases-caucasus-p212-p218-crosscopy), so the whole seven-part assembly remains unresolved.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p212-medical-fragment-exact-account-and-limits"></a>

### Exact account and limits

| Account | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Original observed coordinates, all retained in order | 197 |
| Conditional frame / plaintext positions | 302 / 151 |
| Fixed raw / edited positions | 46 / 129 |
| Proposed lexical positions / other retained raw labels | 121 / 8 |
| Added prefix slots / filled / unassigned | 105 / 83 / 22 |
| Observed substitutions, printed-mask fills, exclusions or reorderings | 0 |

These are lexical proposals, not uniquely forced completions. Each newly fixed label consumes one missing-half fill. An arbitrary full [reencryption witness](../../experiments/p212_medical_fragment/certificates.json) proves compatibility with every original coordinate; its remaining 22 supplied values are not part of the reading.

The frame emerged from **6,300 half-coordinate-aware hypotheses**: 25 registered keys and every even total from 198 to 700. Its score was 78.3508, versus 6.9540 for the next length under the same key. In 100 frequency-preserving shuffles, each screened over those lengths under the already selected Nov22–24 key, the largest score was 19.4420. This is a finite same-key comparison, not a global probability of correctness. Three synthetic controls ranked their true lengths 1, 1 and 2; the imperfect result remains recorded.

Word-lattice decoding, independent compatible-word enumeration and source/mapping review support the fragments. They do not authenticate the missing transmission or prove a unique complete text. [Inputs and method](../../experiments/p212_medical_fragment/README.md) retain the neighboring-length checks, control witnesses and diagnostic limits.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p212-medical-fragment-optional-lexical-extension-hospital-support-staff"></a>

### Optional lexical extension: hospital support staff

A separate [optional six-half proposal](../../experiments/p212_medical_fragment/optional_underpersonal.json) extends positions 95–124 to `MITUNTERPERSONALUMEDIKAMENTEN`. It preserves the primary edition and every observed coordinate, adding only six missing-half values at plaintext positions 96, 97, 98, 99, 100 and 111.

**Optional edited output — 135/151 positions; 89 total inserted-half fills; 16 unresolved:**

`LAZARETT???ANSTALTENDORTHINBEKANNTZUGEBENXWOKRANKEVERBLEIBENKOENNENX3X???9????TRANSPORT???YA???MITUNTERPERSONALUMEDIKAMENTENZUTEILENLASSENUNDIN9EDEMZUG`

**Optional readable German — U expanded as u[nd]; literal 9 retained:** mit Unterpersonal u[nd] Medikamenten zuteilen lassen und in9edem Zug.

| Optional account | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Additional missing-half fills / total fills / unassigned slots | 6 / 89 / 16 |
| Observed-coordinate substitutions / source-mask fills | 0 / 0 |

The term *Unterpersonal* has independent period medical support. [Kowalk's fourth enlarged edition, Berlin 1898, printed p162 / PDF page 186](https://storage.lib.uchicago.edu/pres/2015/pres2015-0552.pdf) uses it after describing hospital attendants, servants, heating, cooking and laundry staff. [Die Gartenlaube, no. 2 (1879), p39](https://de.wikisource.org/wiki/Seite:Die_Gartenlaube_(1879)_039.jpg) likewise applies it to a hospital's cook and ward attendants. The original pages and title metadata were visually checked; compact hashes and crop recipes are in the optional file, with no added images.

Those examples support the meaning **hospital auxiliary/support staff**. They do not witness this telegram or prove its missing text. The U-to-u[nd] expansion remains editorial, and the unresolved joins and literal 9 remain. Verify this layer separately with `python experiments/p212_medical_fragment/verify_optional_underpersonal.py --verify`.

The baseline output keeps `3XX`, both 9 labels and Y literal. A separate conditional interpretation reuses the [published numeric+J conjunction](../../experiments/nov22_nikolajew_constraint/README.md): clear all unproved numeral/J/Q/Y cells, then assign raw Y→1, J→2, 2→6 and 9→J. The [new optional certificate](../../experiments/p212_medical_fragment/optional_transport_extension.json) supplies one globally injective full-square and reencryption witness. It interprets only positions 71–151; `3XX` is not identified as a historical instruction number.

**Conditional readable German — positions 71–151, end exclusive; published numeric+J assumptions:** Zu jedem Transportzug 1 Arzt mit Unterpersonal u[nd] Medikamenten zuteilen lassen und in jedem Zug […]

This proposes arranging a doctor with support staff and medicines for each transport train. The excerpt ends mid-clause; the continuation is not supplied. It remains a lexical and key-interpretation hypothesis, not a uniquely recovered historical sentence. In particular, `ZUGYACHT` also fits the surviving coordinates; the certificate preserves that counterexample. Verify the 13 fills, unchanged earlier layers and global square separately with `python experiments/p212_medical_fragment/verify_optional_transport_extension.py --verify`.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p212-medical-fragment-reproduce-and-attribution"></a>

### Reproduce and attribution

```sh
python experiments/p212_medical_fragment/verify.py --verify
python experiments/p212_medical_fragment/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The standard-library verifier checks the actual displays, all 151 domains, source mappings, 83 fills, 22 unresolved positions and forward witnesses. The PDF option authenticates the existing crop with PyMuPDF and Pillow. Search scores are frozen diagnostics; default verification does not replay the external language model.

Historical key: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and Lasry's 2017 key list. New source review, retrieval, conditional edition and exact accounting: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Earlier source editions retain their credits; no first historical decipherment claim is made.
